objectives: This course is designed to give students a variety of modern macroeconomic theories which help students to hold the current macroeconomic issues and train students’ thinking and logic ability. The course concentrates on short-run fluctuations with an emphasis on the roles of fiscal policy and monetary policy. It then turns to the models of economic growth in the long-run.
content:
1	Introduction
2	Dynamics
3	Investment
4	New Keynesian Economics I
5	New Keynesian Economics II
6	Review
7	Midterm Exam
8	The Solow Growth Model
9	Endogenous Growth I
10	Endogenous Growth II
11	R＆D I
12	R＆D II
13    Real Business Cycles I
14    Real Business Cycles II
15	Review
16	Final Exam
books:
B. J. Heijdra (2009), The Foundations of Modern Macroeconomics, 3rd edition.
N. G. Mankiw (2016), Macroecnomics, 9th edition.
D. Romer (2019), Advanced Macroeconomics, 5th edition.
